title: A/P Detail: a vendor credit shows its own date as its Due Date
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Vendor {Vendor-A} has one unused vendor credit, {Vendor-credit-A}, on today's date.
    For example: {Vendor-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-24 Parts Co; {Vendor-credit-A} is dated 12 days ago.
  • Starting screen: A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Expand the bucket that holds {Vendor-credit-A}.
  2. Read {Vendor-credit-A}'s Date and Due Date cells.
  3. Click the "Due Date" header twice.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the bucket opens and lists {Vendor-credit-A}.
  • Step 2: the Due Date is not blank: it shows the same date as the Date column, as today.
  • Step 3: {Vendor-credit-A} sorts by that date like any other row; it is not held at the bottom.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R6: “A blank value (for example a vendor credit on A/P Unpaid Invoices, which has no due date and no Past Due) sorts to the bottom of its group in both directions. On A/P Detail a vendor credit shows its own date as its due date, as today, so it is not blank there.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). The design draws no picture of this behaviour (all 7 boards and 45 figures checked); the case follows the PRD.
